blocks.etymology: From team + work. Compare West Frisian teamwurk (“teamwork”).

senses.definition: The activity of working together with other people effectively to achieve an objective.

examples.en: Good teamwork was key to our project's success.
examples.vi: Làm việc nhóm hiệu quả là chìa khóa cho thành công của dự án chúng tôi.

senses.vi: sự làm việc nhóm; tinh thần đồng đội

thesaurus.definition: cooperative work done by a team (especially when it is effective)

wiktionary.gloss: The cooperative effort of a team of people to achieve a common goal.

idioms.gloss: It is easier to achieve major goals when working as a team.

blocks.etymology: Origin unknown. Other proverbs with the same meaning referencing the killing of animals are also attested, some as early as the 17th century; see, for example, “there are more ways to kill a dog than hanging” (1678), “there is more than one way to kill a cat” (1833), and “more ways of killing a cat than choking her with cream” (1855).

wiktionary.gloss: A problem generally has more than one solution; there is more than one way to achieve a goal.

there's more than one way to skin a cat.word: there's more than one way to skin a cat

thesaurus.definition: visual impairment involving a loss of peripheral vision

examples: Some people experience tunnel vision during a panic attack.
It took some time for him to get used to the tunnel vision he experienced while looking through a periscope.
wiktionary.gloss: A restricted field of vision, especially as the result of looking through some type of object or a medical condition.

examples: After Mark fell victim to tunnel vision, nothing you could say to him would change his mind.
wiktionary.gloss: The tendency to focus one's attention on one specific idea or viewpoint, to the exclusion of everything else.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English visual, from French visuel, visual and directly from Late Latin vīsuālis (“of sight”), from vīsus (“sight, vision”) + -ālis (“adjective suffix”), from vidēre (“to see, perceive; look (at)”); see visage. By surface analysis, Latin vīsus + -ual.

senses.definition: connected with seeing or the sense of sight.

examples.en: Pictures give strong visual support to young learners.
examples.vi: Hình ảnh mang lại sự hỗ trợ trực quan mạnh mẽ cho học sinh nhỏ tuổi.

examples.en: The artist created an impressive visual effect.
examples.vi: Nghệ sĩ đã tạo ra một hiệu ứng thị giác ấn tượng.

thesaurus.definition: relating to or using sight
visible

wiktionary.gloss: Related to or affecting the vision.

blocks.etymology: From Middle English visual, from French visuel, visual and directly from Late Latin vīsuālis (“of sight”), from vīsus (“sight, vision”) + -ālis (“adjective suffix”), from vidēre (“to see, perceive; look (at)”); see visage. By surface analysis, Latin vīsus + -ual.

senses.definition: a picture, slide, or video used to explain something or add interest.

examples.en: The presentation had great visuals that kept everyone interested.

senses.vi: hình ảnh trực quan; tài liệu trực quan

wiktionary.gloss: Any element of something that depends on sight.
An image; a picture; a graphic.
All the visual elements of a multimedia presentation or entertainment, usually in contrast with normal text or audio.
A preliminary sketch.

examples: The visual where the trombone all threw their instruments into the air looked good.
wiktionary.gloss: Any element of a show done by a marching band besides the marching and playing of instruments.
A hallucination perceived as seen by the eyes, such as from psilocybin.
